The second light.

SurfaceNet runs two offline INT8 defect profiles on Arm Android. An operator can change the light with the rear torch and compare registered defect masks before recording a decision. Llama 3.2 provides the operator procedure through ExecuTorch on the same device.

Four-view thresholds and context weight were selected on 466 training-validation images. Each profile was timed over 120 warmed forwards. The counts represent single-image scores. Live Android additionally uses fixture, temporal and reference checks.

Why four views

The program flips the same exposure across both axes, runs one batched forward pass, aligns the four maps, and averages logits. It reuses the same trained weights. One original exposure plus three reflections remains one optical measurement.

Why a second light

The independently acquired torch image tests whether the same pixels remain abnormal after relighting. On simulated pairs, 88 of 96 initial true alerts and 11 of 24 false alerts were confirmed by the four-view mask gate. Physical-fixture repeatability and sustained phone performance still require measurement.
